h: "As Though I Had Gone into Exile": The Sukkah and Bavel

p: In the text of the "Yehi Ratzon"
"And in the merit of my going out of my house to the outside,
count it for me by this
as though I had wandered far away."
And there are versions that are more explicit:
"And if I have become liable to exile,
let it be counted for me
as though I had wandered far away."
that the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah
וְהַמִּצְטַעֵר פָּטוּר מִן הַסּוּכָּה (סֻכָּה כו, א).
and one who is distressed is exempt from the sukkah (Sukkah 26a).
However, the source of the text
for it is stated in the Pesikta
"The mitzvah of sukkah comes after Yom Kippur:
after the sins have been forgiven,
perhaps they have become liable to exile;
let the mitzvah of sukkah be like the exile of Bavel,
'And you shall come to Bavel; there you shall be rescued,
and from there Hashem will redeem you
from the hand of all your enemies.'"
And to understand why it mentions
However, the exile of Bavel alludes
to this, that the whole matter of the exile
is only for the good and the salvation of Yisrael,
as it was in the exile of Bavel:
הַתְחָלַת יַגְדִּיל תּוֹרָה וְיַאְדִּיר (יְשַׁעְיָה מב, כא),
the beginning of "He will make the Torah great and glorious" (Yeshayah 42:21),
and Yisrael merited more in Bavel
than they had merited in the Land.
from our holy master, teacher and Rebbe,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
that when they were exiled to Bavel,
all of them went in bitterness of soul,
while Yechezkel went with great joy.
that the Holy One, blessed be He, would make shine
more than when they dwelt on their own land.
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב ב, ב):
as is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 2b):
and the holy spirit rested upon Yechezkel,
and he saw what he saw,
and all the hosts of heaven and the Chariot,
who has come to dwell among you,' etc.
and they were not concerned about their exile at all,
דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לָא שָׁבִיק לוֹן,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not abandon them,
and there the Shechinah is with them."
the spreading of the words of the Torah she'b'al peh.
And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said
"Many tzaddikim I raised up in her destruction,
more than when she was settled";
and "Many decrees I decreed upon myself and fulfilled them,
יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁגָּזַרְתָּ עָלַי (עֵירוּבִין כא, ב).
more than what You decreed upon me" (Eruvin 21b).
And all of this came from the Men of the Great Assembly,
For all the decrees and fences
about which it is not stated who made them,
all of them are from the Men of the Great Assembly,
for the sake of the holiness of Yisrael,
And we find in the Mishnah (Avos 1:2):
was among the last of the Men of the Great Assembly";
and make a fence for the Torah" —
for they gave over their very lives
And we find that in the days of Achashverosh,
the Torah she'b'al peh of their own will,
out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He.
For the holding of the mountain over them at Sinai
was over the Torah she'b'al peh
which they did not want to accept of their own will,
and rejecting the pleasure of this world.
they accepted upon themselves the Torah she'b'al peh
that the entire Torah she'b'al peh
was revealed to them in the exile of Bavel,
And the exile itself brought about for Yisrael
the spreading of the holy Torah,
"For in much wisdom is much anger" —
brings about the revelation of abundant wisdom,
And this is why it brings the verse
from the hand of all your enemies":
And through the words of Torah
even the "heart of the fool" is rectified,
for the Holy One, blessed be He.
And likewise the mitzvah of sukkah
when Yisrael's sins have been forgiven
and they become a new creation,
drawing close to the Holy One, blessed be He —
that the exile is in order to increase our holiness,
And the sukkah also shields us,
for it is the spreading of the shelter of peace,
וַאֲנַחְנוּ יוֹשְׁבִים בְּסֵתֶר עֶלְיוֹן (תְּהִלִּים צא, א),
and we dwell "in the shelter of the Most High" (Tehillim 91:1),
so that those lying in wait cannot

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 2b (Shemos) — "When they went down to Babylon the heavens opened and holy prophecy rested on Yechezkel… He told Israel: Your Master is here, with all the hosts of heaven… They did not believe him until he had to reveal all he saw… When Israel heard, they did not fear their exile at all, for they knew the Holy One had not abandoned them; and all he revealed, he revealed with permission."

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 21b — “‘New as well as old, my beloved, I have stored away for you’: The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I have imposed many decrees upon myself beyond what You decreed upon me, and I have fulfilled them.” The additional decrees are presented as Israel’s loving offering. The maamar contrasts that motive with Haman’s accusation that separation comes from pride or hatred.

paragraphs.text: Avos 1:2 — "Shimon HaTzaddik was of the remnants of the Men of the Great Assembly. He used to say: On three things the world stands: on Torah, on avodah, and on acts of kindness."

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avot 1:1 — “Moses received Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence for Torah.” The transmission culminates in the assembly whose program Rav Tzadok invokes: the expansion of students and the protection of Torah through a fence.

paragraphs.text: Kesubos 110b — "Rabbi Zeira would avoid Rav Yehudah, because he wished to go up to Eretz Yisrael; for Rav Yehudah said: Whoever goes up from Bavel to Eretz Yisrael transgresses a positive commandment, as it says, 'They shall be carried to Bavel, and there they shall be, until the day that I remember them' (Yirmeyahu 27:22)."
